eras.label: Paleolithic
eras.blurb: The long age of flaked stone tools, fire, and mobile hunter-gatherer life. Dates mark earliest known archaeological evidence and can shift as new finds appear.

eras.label: Lower Paleolithic
eras.blurb: Earliest flaked stone industries, from Lomekwi and Oldowan cores to Acheulean handaxes.

eras.label: Middle Paleolithic
eras.blurb: Prepared-core tools, more reliable fire, pigments, and the first personal ornaments.

eras.label: Upper Paleolithic
eras.blurb: Needles, musical instruments, representational art, and more specialized hunting gear.

eras.label: Mesolithic
eras.blurb: A transitional world of microliths, fishing, and more intensive use of wild resources.

eras.label: Neolithic
eras.blurb: Humanity begins shifting from mobile foraging toward farming, animal domestication, and lasting settlements.

eras.label: Copper Age
eras.blurb: Native copper and early smelting sit beside stone tools as metallurgy begins.

eras.label: Bronze Age
eras.blurb: Tin-bronze, writing, cities, and long-distance trade reshape the eastern Mediterranean and beyond.

eras.label: Iron Age
eras.blurb: Ironworking spreads. Tools and weapons become cheaper to produce and more widely available.

eras.label: Prehistory
eras.blurb: The span before written records — known through archaeology, not contemporary texts.

eras.label: Ancient World
eras.blurb: Cities, states, writing, and classical science from the first urban cultures through late antiquity.

eras.label: Classical Antiquity
eras.blurb: The Mediterranean and neighboring worlds of Greece, Rome, Persia, and their contemporaries.

eras.label: Medieval
eras.blurb: Paper, gunpowder, the compass, and mechanical clocks travel and transform across Afro-Eurasia.

eras.label: Early Modern
eras.blurb: Print, scientific instruments, and global maritime exchange accelerate the circulation of ideas.

eras.label: Modern
eras.blurb: Industry, fossil energy, and laboratory science remake everyday life.

eras.label: Contemporary
eras.blurb: Nuclear energy, spaceflight, computing, and planetary-scale networks.

eras.label: Pre-industrial
eras.blurb: Muscle, water, wind, and wood — technologies that do not yet run on fossil steam.

eras.label: Industrial Revolution
eras.blurb: Steam, factories, mechanized textiles, and iron railways begin the modern energy economy.

eras.label: Second Industrial Revolution
eras.blurb: Electricity, steel, chemicals, telegraphs, and the internal combustion engine.

eras.label: Machine Age
eras.blurb: Mass production, automobiles, aircraft, radio, and the first electronic computers.

eras.label: Atomic Age
eras.blurb: Controlled nuclear chain reactions enter weapons, power, and medicine.

eras.label: Space Age
eras.blurb: Orbital flight, satellites, and human travel beyond Earth.

eras.label: Jet Age
eras.blurb: Jet propulsion makes intercontinental travel routine.

eras.label: Digital Revolution
eras.blurb: From the transistor to personal computing, networks, and the web.

eras.label: Information Age
eras.blurb: Microprocessors, software, and global digital networks become infrastructure.

eras.label: Fourth Industrial Revolution
eras.blurb: Cyber-physical systems, ubiquitous sensing, and machine learning enter industry and daily life.

eras.label: AI Era
eras.blurb: Deep learning and large models make general-purpose machine intelligence a practical technology.
